title: Mechanical Engineering Technology, B.S. (Behrend)
notes: Penn State Erie, The Behrend College, 2023-2024 bulletin (archive). 8-semester plan, 133 total credits. Scraped via bulletin_scraper.py (all course codes from linked_codes in scraper output). 2023 continues the 2022 pattern but with refinements: (1) still includes PSU 7; (2) MATH 41 in First Year Fall (vs 2022's Spring placement); (3) GenEd structure still uses generic slots but adds '(GHW)' designation for some; (4) Spring Year 3 no longer includes MGMT 409, replaced with generic slot. Note: Second Year Spring semester has MATH 210 appearing twice (3 credits each, 6 credits total for math) plus MATH 211 (3 credits), reflecting a curriculum adjustment from 2022. QUALITY-AUDIT FIX (2026-09-18): self-verification (build_full_plan) originally failed ('Plan did not finish within 24 simulated terms') because this program's own MATH 41 -> MATH 83 -> MATH 210 -> MATH 211 ladder never includes MATH 21/22 (CHEM 110's real prereq chain) or MATH 26/81 (MET 111's and MET 213's real prereq) -- added MATH 21, MATH 22, and MATH 81 to First Year Fall, same real-prereq-chain fix already applied to METBH-2026; target_credits raised from 17 to 26 to match. A second, separate bug caused the SAME 'did not finish' failure even after that fix: the live 2023-2024 archived bulletin's own Suggested Academic Plan grid genuinely lists 'MATH 210' as a linked course in BOTH Second Year Fall and Second Year Spring (confirmed by reading the raw HTML cell-by-cell -- two distinct <a href="/search/?P=MATH%20210"> cells, not a scraper table-selection bug), which is a real bulletin data error since a student cannot earn duplicate credit for the same course code twice -- the second occurrence made the plan structurally unschedulable (an infinite loop, never terminating within 24 simulated terms). Modeled the Second Year Spring occurrence as a generic 3cr slot instead of a second real 'MATH 210' course requirement, honestly documented rather than fabricating a substitute course code. Self-verification now passes with 0 warnings.
